title: Mismatch
intro: Two nominally identical transistors differ by small random amounts. This mismatch sets offsets, CMRR and converter accuracy.

blocks.text: Random mismatch has a standard deviation inversely proportional to the square root of device area (Pelgrom's law):

blocks.source: sigma(Delta-VTH) = A_VT / sqrt(W*L)         sigma(Delta-beta / beta) = A_beta / sqrt(W*L)

blocks.text: A_VT is a process constant, typically 1 to 5 mV*um. To halve the mismatch you must quadruple the area, which raises capacitance. Systematic mismatch from gradients and layout asymmetry is separate and is addressed in layout (common-centroid, same orientation).

blocks.title: Pelgrom's law
blocks.text: A_VT = 5 mV*um. Find sigma(Delta-VTH) for W*L = 1 um^2 and 25 um^2.

blocks.title: Effect on a current mirror
blocks.text: Two mirror transistors have Vov = 0.2 V and sigma(Delta-VTH) = 2 mV. What current mismatch results (to first order)?
solution: Delta-I / I = 2 * Delta-VTH / Vov = 2 * 2 mV / 0.2 V = 2 percent.
